subject: Post-call recap: Integration acceptance criteria + onboarding roadmap
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@olivetech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2025 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Integration acceptance criteria + onboarding roadmap

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear signals on priorities. Below is a compact recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and an initial onboarding roadmap + owners. Please flag anything I missed or mischaracterized.

Quick summary of pain & goals
- High concurrent inference traffic from chat UI (peaks ~350 RPS during business hours).
- Current infra: Kubernetes (EKS), services in Node.js + a Python microservice for ML pre/post-processing, image pipeline on GCS.
- Primary pain: unpredictable latency spikes and high per-token cost with current hosted model provider.
- Goal: reduce 95th latency to under 200ms and lower cost per active conversation while keeping response quality equivalent.

Key technical constraints
- Must support OpenAI-compatible REST API surface (existing wrapper assumes OpenAI endpoints).
- Prefer SDKs for Python first, Go second; Node.js team can iterate later.
- VPC peering or private connectivity mandatory for production (we discussed an initial NAT workaround for PoC).

Success criteria for PoC (consensus items)
1) Functional parity: same prompt/response format and tokenization behavior with <5% quality delta measured on the seed eval set.
2) Latency: end-to-end 95th percentile < 200ms for 256-token interactions at 150 RPS sustained.
3) Cost: demonstrable reduction in per-1000-token cost compared to current vendor (benchmarks to be provided).
4) Security: evidence of data handling & retention, SOC2 attestation or equivalent; initial security questionnaire (attached).

Technical onboarding plan & milestones (owner — ETA)
- Discovery -> Technical deep-dive (Neha + Vivek) — 1 week (owner: Neha)
- Provision PoC environment (dev VPC + test keys) — 2 weeks (owner: Vivek)
- Integration: SDK + example client (Python + Go) and OpenAI-compatible endpoint validation — 2 weeks (owner: Marissa)
- Load test + cost benchmark run (150–200 RPS) — 1 week (owner: Marissa)
- End-to-end evaluation & acceptance (Olive Tech QA) — 1 week (owner: Linda)

Deliverables we will share after this email
- Draft PoC SOW (attached: PoC-SOW-Outline.pdf)
- Integration checklist (attached)
- Example Python snippet + OpenAI-compatible cURL examples

Immediate next steps
- Linda: confirm the three success criteria above and any additional security evidence needed (you mentioned a data flow diagram).
- Rajesh: confirm preferred sample data set and a safe test queue for load testing.
- Vivek: will spin up a dev endpoint and share credentials for integration testing.
- I'll send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive next Tue (Nov 18) — 60 minutes.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: PoC-SOW-Outline.pdf (6 pages); redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx
From: Linda Park <linda@olivetech.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Malhotra <rajesh@olivetech.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2025 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Integration acceptance criteria + onboarding roadmap

Neha — thanks for the thorough recap. This looks accurate and helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: we agree with the four bullets. Add one more: automated fallback/rollback if latency > 400ms for 2 consecutive minutes during the test window.
- Security: joining our security lead will be helpful — attaching our internal questionnaire (security-questionnaire-olivetech.docx). SOC2 is a must for production.
- SDKs: Python first is correct. Rajesh prefers Go client as the second priority; Node can be deprioritized for the PoC.

Rajesh will provision a small, anonymized sample payload (redacted). We'll have that ready by Mon EOD. Also, can you confirm whether private connectivity (VPC peering) is required for the PoC or if we can use token-based access from our staging environment? We want the fastest path to start.

One logistical ask: can you share a one-page runbook for how Redwood handles model rollbacks and incident contact during the PoC?

-Linda
Linda Park
Product Manager, Olive Tech
linda@olivetech.com

Attachment stub: security-questionnaire-olivetech.docx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@olivetech.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Integration acceptance criteria + onboarding roadmap

Thanks — quick technical notes: 
1) For PoC we can start with token-based staging access (fastest). We recommend private connectivity for the production cutover; will outline timelines.
2) Python SDK: we'll share a 0.1.0 preview package with examples today. Go client alpha will follow next week.
3) Rollback/runbook: attached one-pager in the Drive link (see related links). Key points: blue-green endpoints, automatic fallbacks to a smaller model, and 24/7 on-call escalation with an SRE contact list.

I'll provision a dev endpoint and send test keys by EOD Monday (Nov 17). Vivek (Tech Lead, Redwood) — will own the dev endpoint + load test execution.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@olivetech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Integration acceptance criteria + onboarding roadmap

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmations and Rajesh for the data prep. Next steps on my side:
- Share calendar invite for Tue Nov 18 10:00am PT (technical deep-dive).
- Send the preliminary PoC SOW via DocuSign for review (link will follow).
- Marissa will post the example Python snippet and a short test harness repo in the shared Drive.

If there are no objections, we'll start the token-based PoC tomorrow and pivot to private connectivity for the production stretch. I'll also attach the rollback one-pager to the SOW send.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Neha
